current_main.144: [Calculated] Principal findings: drug-resistance markers. The previous version's resistance findings were affected by a defect in how markers were identified - the panel matched SnpEff protein-change strings, which can see neither a resistance allele that is itself the reference residue nor a residue that requires two nucleotide changes in one codon - and the panel has been rebuilt by codon reconstruction, which corrects it. Two findings follow directly from the rebuild. pfdhps A437G, wholly absent from the previous panel, stands at 0.897 for G437 (n = 1,892; deciduous forest 0.964, coastal savanna 0.941, Guinea savanna 0.875, transitional zone 0.800; chi-square p = 1.2 x 10 to the -6); the official Pf8 methodology states that the 3D7 sequence translates as a G at 437 and that this is the mutant allele, so the resistance residue is the reference residue and no ALT annotation for it can exist. And the former "naming discrepancy" at pfcrt 75 was never a naming matter: N75E requires two SNPs in one codon (403621 A>G, annotated Asn75Asp; 403623 T>A, annotated Asn75Lys), and neither annotation names it. Haplotypes are now counted within isolates on complete cases. The pfdhfr IRN triple mutant is 0.771 (n = 1,876; 95% CI 0.751-0.789) - not the marginal range 0.786-0.908 previously quoted, and, as it must be, below its lowest component on the same complete-case set (51I = 0.788); NRN sits at 0.116 and the fully wild-type NCS at 0.091, so it is not a near-fixed single haplotype, and the quadruple IRNL is 0.000. pfcrt CVIET is 0.071 and is demonstrably a single unit: only CVMNK (0.929) and CVIET occur at codons 72-76, with nothing intermediate. pfdhps GE (437G + 540E) is 0.010. The pfdhfr marginals remain high and lowest in Guinea savanna (S108N 0.908 overall / 0.885 Guinea savanna; C59R 0.886 / 0.864; N51I 0.786 / 0.764; chi-square p = 9.4 x 10 to the -7, 4.8 x 10 to the -5 and 2.4 x 10 to the -4), with the transitional zone (n = 25) at or near the top of all three. The pfk13 panel was rebuilt from the WHO compendium v1.0 (December 2025) and covers all 14 validated markers (F446I, N458Y, C469Y, M476I, Y493H, G533S, R539T, I543T, P553L, R561H, P574L, C580Y, R622I, A675V) and all 6 candidates (E252Q, P441L, C469F, N537I, G538V, V568G); the old list was written from memory, misclassified P441L and C469F as validated when WHO classes them as candidate, and omitted P574L, G533S and R622I. All 23 pfk13 codons carry no screened resistance allele: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue, and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon of 1,900, across a 2009-2021 sampling period - a tested historical negative, not a statement about the present. Validation is now per sample rather than per marginal frequency: 47,012 of 47,012 calls agree with MalariaGEN's published genotypes, 100.0000% across 25 markers, codon 75 included.
current_main.170: Answered, on a rebuilt panel. 19 XtX outliers above the calibrated threshold, 13 of which pass FDR 10%. Seventeen of the 19 fall in 13 annotated genes; two are intergenic, including one (XtX 20.79, q = 0.005) that ranks fifth overall and survives FDR correction. The set is not an artefact - every significant quality difference favours the outliers (VQSLOD p = 0.008, QD p = 0.016, QUAL p = 0.007), none has MQ < 50, strand bias or read-position bias, all 19 are RegionType Core, and the eight exported-protein SNPs are the cleanest subset in the panel - but two adjacent chromosome-11 sites, that fifth-ranked intergenic SNP and SNRPF Pf3D7_11_v3:1,054,078 (q = 0.031), are downgraded to lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. pfaat1 Ser258Leu falls from 0.824 in coastal savanna to 0.544 in Guinea savanna (chi-square p = 1.9 x 10 to the -18). pfdhps G437 - a locus absent from the superseded panel - stands at 0.897 (n = 1,892; p = 1.2 x 10 to the -6). The pfdhfr IRN haplotype is 0.771 on complete cases (n = 1,876; CI 0.751-0.789), not the 0.79-0.91 marginal range previously quoted, and pfcrt CVIET is 0.071. All 23 pfk13 codons - covering the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates, which between them occupy 19 distinct codons - carry no screened resistance allele: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue, and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y. The denominators are 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon, over 2009-2021. Agreement with MalariaGEN is 47,012 of 47,012 calls across 25 markers.
current_main.854: The pfk13 negative, stated with its two limits. All 23 pfk13 codons carry no screened resistance allele in any isolate with a call, twenty-two of them at the reference residue in every called isolate and codon 458 at 0.9995, and the twenty-third, codon 458, carries a single isolate with Asn458Asp — which is not the validated variant at that codon, N458Y — giving the reference residue a frequency of 0.9995 over 1,866 called isolates. No validated or candidate artemisinin-resistance residue was observed at any codon. Two limits must travel with that statement. First, the denominator is per codon, 1,845 to 1,876 of 1,900 across the pfk13 codons (1,834 to 1,900 across the panel as a whole), not "all 1,900 isolates at every codon"; the earlier formulation "all 14 validated pfk13 codons at 0.000 in all 1,900 isolates" is wrong on the codon count, on the denominator and on the panel it was computed from, and is withdrawn. Second, the sampling period is 2009 to 2021, so this is a historical negative and says nothing about the frequency today. What is now defensible, and was not before, is that the negative covers the complete validated set — 14 validated and 6 candidate variants, 20 in all at 19 distinct codons — rather than an incomplete list written from memory, with the tiers kept distinct.
current_main.981: Why one conclusion strengthens while the other falls. The two outcomes are not in tension, and the asymmetry is instructive rather than suspicious. Maximum FST is a point estimate pooled over thousands of sites, so it moves little when the site set or the sample changes, and six scenarios agreeing to within 0.0005 is a genuine stability result. The Mantel p-value is a significance verdict on a correlation over 21 pairwise points from seven populations, and at baseline it sat at 0.0252 — inside the top half of the interval below 0.05, with very little margin. A verdict with that little margin, resting on that few points, is exactly the kind that threshold choices can decide, and here they do. The check shows that the magnitude of measured common-variant differentiation is stable across the tested thresholds, whereas the significance of the distance correlation is not; it does not estimate panmixia.
current_main.3198: [Interpreted] It cannot establish that the retained panel is neutral, because no neutral mask was ever defined. The 3,916 SNPs are the sites that survived the FILTER_PASS, biallelic-SNP, missingness and minor-allele-frequency criteria, and not one of those is a neutrality criterion: no coding or non-coding partition, no synonymous/non-synonymous distinction, no gene-proximity exclusion and no recombination-rate weighting was applied at any stage. The panel therefore contains the resistance loci themselves — the XtX scan is run on this same panel and returns pfaat1 and PTP7 from it — so the set used to measure background differentiation also contains the sites under the strongest selection in the genome. That inclusion is very unlikely to be driving the differentiation result: 19 outliers among 3,916 sites cannot move a ratio-of-averages estimator away from 0.002, and the maximum FST is stable at 0.00204–0.00255 across six scenarios that change the panel composition substantially. The point is not that the number is wrong but that the word is unearned. Wherever “neutral” appears in this report it should be read as “genome-wide at the retained common variants”, never as “at sites shown to be free of selection”. Building a genuine neutral mask — excluding the known resistance loci, the antigenic and invasion gene families, and sites in high linkage with them, then recomputing differentiation on what remains — is a specified next step and is not done here.
current_main.3211: [Interpreted] What the retained common-variant result licenses. Differentiation between zones is very low but detectable — maximum pairwise FST 0.00232, with one of six confidence intervals spanning zero (Guinea savanna vs transitional zone, [−0.00083, 0.00178]), and the maximum staying within 0.00204–0.00255 across six threshold scenarios (Table 8.3) — but this does not establish that sparse sampling adequately characterises population structure. Marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the rebuilt resistance panel shows significant between-zone variation at six of the nine panel genes, including pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1 (the others being pfcrt, pfmdr1 and pfmdr2). Whether a handful of sites represents the country's genomic background is not answered by a low differentiation estimate; the measured marker-frequency heterogeneity also argues against assuming that those sites represent resistance-marker frequencies.
current_main.3213: [Observed] The resistance panel settles the question empirically, and the answer is no. Marker frequencies do differ by zone. pfaat1 S258L spans about 28 percentage points from coast to far north (0.824 to 0.544, χ² p = 1.89 × 10⁻¹⁸, n = 1,896 called). pfdhps G437 — the allele that was missing from the panel altogether in the previous draft — runs 0.964 in deciduous forest and 0.941 on the coast against 0.875 in Guinea savanna and 0.800 in the transitional zone (χ² p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶, n = 1,892). The pfdhfr codons are heterogeneous across the four zones (S108N χ² p = 9.4 × 10⁻⁷; C59R 4.8 × 10⁻⁵; N51I 2.4 × 10⁻⁴) and the IRN triple-mutant haplotype itself runs 0.750 in Guinea savanna, 0.788 in deciduous forest, 0.867 on the coast and 0.880 in the transitional zone on 25 isolates. These are all four-zone heterogeneity tests; no directional south-versus-Guinea contrast was run, and the transitional zone's values rest on 25 isolates (§7.2). A sentinel site on the coast and a sentinel site in Upper East would report materially different resistance-marker profiles despite very low differentiation among the sampled groups at retained common variants. The operational implication is the reverse of the previous draft's: low common-variant differentiation alone does not establish that sparse sampling characterises either population structure or marker frequencies. A surveillance design intended to track resistance needs to span the gradient, and this analysis is evidence for rather than against that requirement.
current_main.3217: [Proposed] The unqualified surveillance claim must be removed wherever it is restated. There is no section titled "plain-language summary" in this manuscript; the nearest equivalents are the Abstract's concluding sentence, which reproduced the claim without even the caveat above, and the positive-findings list in §10.1. Both must carry the qualified form given in the first paragraph of this section — very low but detectable common-variant differentiation, with neither population-structure nor marker-frequency representativeness established by sparse sampling — and not the unqualified one. This is the clearest case in the document of a conclusion that the corrected resistance panel reverses, so the three locations must not disagree. The same applies to isolation by distance: any statement of it in the Abstract or in §10.1 must now carry the 2-of-6 grading, not a "weak but real" one.

current_main.3527: This section has now been rewritten twice and revised a third time. The first rewrite followed an internal adversarial audit; this one follows an external critique of 10 October 2026 whose five points were all upheld, four of them identifying defects in the analysis code rather than in the prose. The defect that matters here is that the first corrected resistance panel was itself wrong: it found markers by matching SnpEff ANN_HGVS_p protein-change strings against a hand-written list, which cannot see a resistance allele that is the reference residue and cannot see a residue reached by two changes in one codon. A new script, scripts/step12_codon_panel.py, reconstructs each codon from the CDS and the reference genome and replaces the panel entirely. The following statements are therefore withdrawn from the previous version and should not be quoted from it: the pfdhfr triple mutant as "0.786–0.908"; the claim that pfk13 was tested at 14 validated codons "in all 1,900 isolates"; the classification of P441L and C469F as validated; the "marker-naming discrepancy" at pfcrt codon 75; the validation claim "21 of 23 markers agree within 0.03"; the description of pfaat1 S258L as "the functionally validated chloroquine-resistance variant"; and the statement that nothing in the functional work tested amodiaquine. The population-genetic results below are unchanged and were read from the corrected run of 10 October 2026 (3,916 SNPs x 1,900 isolates, mean missingness 0.0295); every resistance number below was read from step12's own outputs. A third round followed on the same date and is recorded in Appendix F: the four robustness checks that this section's own next-steps list carried as outstanding were run, and one of them overturned a conclusion instead of confirming it. Isolation by distance is withdrawn as a supported result and is reported below as not robust. The evidence that measured common-variant differentiation is stable across the tested thresholds is strengthened by the same six scenarios. Nothing in the resistance panel is touched by these checks, and the withdrawals listed above stand exactly as they are.
current_main.3606: [Interpreted] What this implies for surveillance design, stated narrowly. Differentiation among the sampled zones is very low but detectable at retained common variants; that result does not show that a spatially sparse design adequately characterises population structure. The lack of a robust isolation-by-distance result does not validate a sparse sampling design. Marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and it is the question sentinel surveillance actually answers; on that question this analysis finds significant between-zone variation at pfdhps 437 (p = 1.2 x 10-6), pfdhfr (p <= 2.43 x 10-4 at all three triple-mutant codons; the largest of the three is 2.425 x 10-4 at Asn51Ile) and pfaat1 (p = 1.9 x 10-18). The original Section 7.4 conclusion — that sentinel surveillance at a small number of sites is an adequate design for detecting emergence — is therefore withdrawn in its unqualified form, here and in Section 7.4. This is the clearest case in the manuscript of a conclusion that the resistance panel reverses, and the two sections must not disagree.
current_main.3607: Robustness, where it stops, and the one conclusion it removed. The population-genetic conclusions did not change when the SNP panel grew by 16.6 per cent, the BayPass scan became reproducible and false-discovery accounting was added — and one of them has now been tested against the two thresholds that define the dataset and did change. What survived: maximum FST stayed within 0.00204–0.00255 across six threshold scenarios spanning 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs; the ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve stayed near-flat with a negligible K = 2 improvement; re-running the ordinations on the analysis set left the silhouette slightly more negative rather than less; and the 19 outliers came through a quality check with every significant difference in their favour, though two chromosome-11 sites are downgraded on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal the check itself surfaced. What did not survive: isolation by distance, significant in two of six threshold scenarios and four of seven region jackknife replicates, now reported as not robust. Near-panmixia and isolation by distance were graded together in the previous version, both under "robust to the largest correction the pipeline received"; they are not the same kind of result and the same six scenarios separate them cleanly. The resistance results are a third case and should not be described as robust in the same sentence as either: the first correction created the finding and the second changed its content. The triple mutant moved from an implied 0.786–0.908 to a measured 0.771, a locus at 0.897 appeared that had been absent altogether, two pfk13 variants were reclassified, a marker discrepancy dissolved into an annotation bug, and the central functional interpretation was reversed. Two successive corrections in the same place is itself a result about the process, recorded in Appendix F. The threshold sensitivity was not run on the codon panel, so nothing is claimed about the resistance frequencies' behaviour under other thresholds.

current_main.3977: [Observed] This appendix exists for traceability, and it now records three rounds. Round one, 9–10 October 2026: an adversarial multi-agent audit. Eight reviewers working across separate dimensions raised 110 findings, each of which was then put to three independent verifiers prompted to refute it and defaulting to refuted where they could not substantiate the claim. A finding counts as confirmed only where at least two of three verifiers failed to refute it after checking the code, data or outputs themselves. Sixty-one findings were confirmed — 14 high severity, 31 medium, 16 low — with 19 disputed and 21 refuted. Thirty verifications in the reproducibility dimension were lost to a rate limit and are recorded as unverified rather than confirmed. Seven confirmed defects required code changes; stages 4 to 9 were re-run on 10 October 2026 with all seven in place. Round two, 10 October 2026: an external critique of the corrected manuscript. It raised five points. All five were upheld and four were defects in the analysis code, not in the prose — in the resistance panel that round one had introduced to fix its own largest finding. The panel was rebuilt as scripts/step12_codon_panel.py and every resistance number in this revision was read from that script's outputs. This is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect, and the pattern is consistent: each layer was checked for internal consistency against our own outputs, and what escaped was external correctness — whether the marker list matched an authoritative source, whether the annotation direction matched the reference genome, whether a co-occurrence claim had co-occurrence data behind it. The verification architecture was built to catch stale numbers, and it did. It was not built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. Round three, 10 October 2026: the four outstanding robustness checks. This round was not an audit of the manuscript but the execution of four items that Section 10.4 carried as outstanding, and it is recorded here because one of them overturned a conclusion instead of confirming it. The Fws and MAF sensitivity analysis (scripts/step13_sensitivity.py) withdrew isolation by distance as a supported result — significant in two of six threshold scenarios — and, from the same six runs, was initially described as making near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript. That earlier label is now withdrawn: the six runs establish stability of measured common-variant differentiation, not the mating system. The outlier quality check cleared the exported-protein artefact concern and downgraded two chromosome-11 SNPs on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal. Stage 3 was re-run on the analysis set. The GeoJSON provenance cannot be closed analytically and remains open. Round three found no defect in the prose and none in the analysis code; what it found was that a published result depended on the thresholds that produced it. Two integrity incidents occurred during the round and are registered as rows 13 and 14 of Table F.1 rather than left in the logs.

current_supplement_target_cells.3632: Yes, and the panel behind this answer has now been rebuilt twice. pfdhps G437 is 0.897 overall and zone-structured (0.964 deciduous forest, 0.941 coastal savanna, 0.875 Guinea savanna, 0.800 transitional; p = 1.2 x 10-6) - a locus absent from the previous panel entirely, because the resistance residue is the 3D7 reference residue. pfaat1 S258L runs 0.824 coastal to 0.544 Guinea savanna (p = 1.9 x 10-18, n = 1,896). The pfdhfr triple-mutant haplotype IRN is 0.771 on 1,876 complete cases (CI 0.751-0.789), not the 0.786-0.908 marginal range previously quoted, with NRN 0.116 and wild-type NCS 0.091; its component codons differ across zones at p <= 2.43 x 10-4 (the largest of the three being 2.425 x 10-4 at Asn51Ile). pfcrt CVIET is 0.071 and is genuinely a unit: only CVMNK (0.929) and CVIET occur. All 23 pfk13 codons - all 14 WHO-validated and all 6 candidate variants, which share codon 469 and so occupy 19 codons, plus four potential-tier codons - are fixed at the reference residue (codon 458 at 0.9995, its single alternative call being Asn458Asp and not the validated N458Y) on 1,845-1,876 called isolates per codon, over 2009-2021. This question was originally reported as null; the null was a filter artefact, and the first correction of it was itself incomplete.
current_supplement_target_cells.3611: Robustness, where it stops, and the one conclusion it removed. The population-genetic conclusions did not change when the SNP panel grew by 16.6 per cent, the BayPass scan became reproducible and false-discovery accounting was added — and one of them has now been tested against the two thresholds that define the dataset and did change. What survived: maximum FST stayed within 0.00204–0.00255 across six threshold scenarios spanning 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs; the ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve stayed near-flat with a negligible K = 2 improvement; re-running the ordinations on the analysis set left the silhouette slightly more negative rather than less; and the 19 outliers came through a quality check with every significant difference in their favour, though two chromosome-11 sites are downgraded on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal the check itself surfaced. What did not survive: isolation by distance, significant in two of six threshold scenarios and four of seven region jackknife replicates, now reported as not robust. Near-panmixia and isolation by distance were graded together in the previous version, both under "robust to the largest correction the pipeline received"; they are not the same kind of result and the same six scenarios separate them cleanly. The resistance results are a third case and should not be described as robust in the same sentence as either: the first correction created the finding and the second changed its content. The triple mutant moved from an implied 0.786–0.908 to a measured 0.771, a locus at 0.897 appeared that had been absent altogether, two pfk13 variants were reclassified, a marker discrepancy dissolved into an annotation bug, and the central functional interpretation was reversed. Two successive corrections in the same place is itself a result about the process, recorded in Appendix F. The threshold sensitivity was not run on the codon panel, so nothing is claimed about the resistance frequencies' behaviour under other thresholds.
